findings.summary: `held_back` is chosen separately from `rating`, so the summary can pair one pass's held-back note with another pass's rating.
findings.evidence: display.rs:747 uses `report.held_back.is_some()` to explain a rating taken after a landing ("target not met: held back by the source check"), and display.rs:771-775 prints the held-back line. Suppose pass 1 held back a rating that met the target, and pass 2 lands and takes a new rating below target with no hold-back. Step 2 then keeps the carried `held_back` and the pass's own rating, and the summary claims the source check held back a rating that it did not. Fix: Take `held_back` from the same source as the chosen `rating`: the pass's own when its rating is used, the carried one only when the carried rating is used. Add one assertion for this in the criterion 4 test, or a small unit test of `apply`.
findings.location: Plan step 2 (`Carried::apply`, held_back rule) and Decision 4

findings.summary: Merged `improvement_turns[].dispatch` no longer matches its documented meaning, "which dispatch of the run it was".
findings.evidence: `ImprovementTaken::dispatch` is documented as "Which dispatch of the run it was, counted from 1" (drain.rs:1170). The plan concatenates the turns without renumbering them, so in the merged report two turns can both claim to be dispatch 1 or 2. Fix: Either offset the carried pass's numbers by carrying a dispatched count and adding it, or change the field doc to say the count is per pass after a rebuild. Pick one and state it in the module docs.

findings.summary: The new public `Carried` sits next to an existing private `Carry` struct that means something else.
findings.evidence: drain.rs:1258-1268 already defines `struct Carry` (what one plan keeps for the next inside a run), and `st.carry` is used at drain.rs:2091, 2329 and 2990. Fix: Rename the new type to something like `RunTally` or `CarriedTally` so the two are not confused.

findings.summary: tests/drain.rs:8249-8289 is described as a `follow_restart` test, but it does not call `follow_restart`.
findings.evidence: Searching for `follow_restart` finds calls only at tests/drain.rs:1958 and 2022. The test at 8250 checks `report.restart` and the printed text through `run_with`. Fix: Describe 8250 as a test of `Report::restart`. Coverage is unaffected, because the plan leaves `Restart` untouched.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot using Read and Grep only, and it holds up. Each pass still computes `Restart` from its own State (drain.rs:3115-3131). The plan merges the carry after the pass returns (in `run_pass`), so the budget and job limit handed on stay the same and nothing is counted twice. The carry travels in `drain.carry` in the state directory. Only a process where `PidGuard::acquire` reports `carried_over` keeps it, and that is true only when the pid file names this same pid with the same start marker (drain.rs:3670-3672), which is what an exec leaves. A fresh drain, a `drain-restart` spawn, a recycled pid or a start after a failed exec all delete the file, so they start at zero. Every name the plan cites exists as described: `follow_restart` at 3188, `guarded` at 3720, `write_record` and `PidRecord` are public, the `rebuilding` stub is at tests/drain.rs:1923, `unrelated` routes a landing to crates/ (tests/drain.rs:278-281), and the summary format is at display.rs:731-737. The tests run the real `drain::drain`, `run_pass`, `guarded` and `display::drain`, with only the exec replaced by a closure, and each would fail without the merge or the clearing. The dependents list matches what I found when I searched for readers: commands.rs is the only production caller, plus the doc entry in docs/decisions.md. The soundness concerns are small. `held_back` is carried separately from the rating it explains, and a few details of the plan are cosmetic. None of this blocks the plan.
